quote.text: Where do I keep everyone's allergies and reactions

promise.text: What to put in a family medical binder

lines.text: Eight things to write down for each person, a filled example page, and what belongs in a paper folder instead.

eyebrow.text: Filling in the answers you don't have

head.text: Start with what's in your wallet: the insurance card gives you the insurer, the member ID and the group number.

body.text: Copy it exactly, letters and zeros included.

eyebrow.text: Filling in the answers you don't have

head.text: Pull the medicine names from the labels, not from memory.

body.text: Write the name, the dose as printed, and how often.

eyebrow.text: Filling in the answers you don't have

head.text: Ask the doctor's office and the pharmacy for their phone numbers if you don't have them saved, and write down which one is which.

eyebrow.text: Filling in the answers you don't have

head.text: For vaccines, ask the clinic that gave them for a copy of the record, then type the names and dates in as written.

body.text: If a clinic is gone, the CDC says it doesn't hold vaccination records itself, and points you to your state's immunization information system, your provider or your state health department.

eyebrow.text: Filling in the answers you don't have

head.text: Add allergies last, and add what happens as well as what they're allergic to.

body.text: "Peanuts (hives)" is something a sitter can use.

line.text: Per person, with what happens recorded alongside, in one place you can reach without a clinic portal login.

title.text: What to put in a family medical binder
